questions.question:
In 1919, Rafael Palma delivered an address advocating for women's suffrage, or right to vote, to the Philippine Senate. Because the debate in the nation around this issue was similar to past debates about women's education, Palma reminded his audience that any concerns were ________: only positive results had arisen from women's education, and the same results would come from women's suffrage.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because the text explains that only positive results had come from women's education and that the same positive outcome would result from women's suffrage. This logic supports the idea that there was no real reason for concern—that is, any worries were unnecessary. Choice A is incorrect because "required" suggests concerns were needed or justified, the opposite of what the passage's logic supports. Choice B is incorrect because "ancient" describes the age of the concerns, not whether they were justified, and nothing in the text discusses how old the concerns were. Choice D is incorrect because "curious" would describe the concerns as strange or odd, which does not match the passage's point that the concerns had no basis given the positive track record of women's education.

questions.question:
Similar to modern tourism websites, an 1890 publication—E. L. Lomax's Oregon, Washington, and Alaska: Sights and Scenes for the Tourist—relates stories of local folklore to potential visitors. In one section of the publication, Lomax tells the legend of The Dalles, where there lived creatures of such ________ size and strength that a strike of their tails could create chasms in the ground.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the legendary creatures are described as having size and strength so great that a single strike of their tails could create chasms—an extraordinary, almost supernatural feat that matches "phenomenal." Choice B is incorrect because "conventional" means ordinary or typical, which directly contradicts the extraordinary effect described (creating chasms in the ground). Choice C is incorrect because "feasible" means possible or achievable, a concept that does not logically describe a creature's size or strength. Choice D is incorrect because "steady" means stable or unchanging, which has no logical connection to the creatures' extraordinary size and destructive strength.

questions.question:
During the late nineteenth century, author Marie Corelli was best known for her use of supernatural and romantic themes in her novels. Despite predictions from critics that Corelli's reliance on sentimental and unrealistic plots would impact the earning potential of her works, Corelli went on to become one of the most ________ writers of her time.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the word "Despite" signals a contrast between the critics' prediction (that her sentimental plots would hurt the earning potential of her books) and what actually happened. The logical contrast to reduced earning potential is that Corelli's books earned a great deal—that is, she became one of the most marketable writers of her time. Choice A is incorrect because "unconventional" merely restates the already-established fact that her themes were supernatural and romantic; it does not create the needed contrast with the critics' prediction about earning potential. Choice B is incorrect because "condemned" does not logically follow from "Despite" a prediction about earning potential—being condemned is not a coherent contrast to reduced sales. Choice C is incorrect because "impressionable" describes a person easily influenced by others, which is unrelated to a writer's commercial success or earning potential.

questions.question:
The following text is adapted from Susan Glaspell's 1916 play Trifles.

MRS PETERS: But of course you were awful busy, Mrs Hale—your house and your children.

MRS HALE: I could've come. I stayed away because it weren't cheerful—and that's why I ought to have come. I—I've never liked this place. Maybe because it's down in a hollow and you don't see the road. I dunno what it is, but it's a lonesome place and always was. I wish I had come over to see Minnie Foster sometimes. I can see now—

MRS PETERS: Well, you mustn't reproach yourself, Mrs Hale. Somehow we just don't see how it is with other folks until—something comes up.

As used in the text, what does the word "reproach" most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because Mrs. Hale has just been blaming herself for not visiting Minnie Foster, and Mrs. Peters tells her not to "reproach" herself, meaning not to blame or criticize herself for this. Choice B is incorrect because "humiliate" implies causing shame in front of others, which is a much stronger and more public act than the private self-blame Mrs. Hale is expressing. Choice C is incorrect because "remind" does not capture the negative, self-blaming tone of Mrs. Hale's guilt; Mrs. Peters is telling her not to blame herself, not telling her not to recall something. Choice D is incorrect because "question" would mean to doubt or interrogate oneself, which does not match the specific act of self-blame that Mrs. Peters is addressing.

choices: A) To discount the theory that glee is a less frequently perceived emotion than hopelessness is
B) To convey how the perceptions of people who experience freedom relate to those who experience imprisonment
C) To consider whether actions taken in confined spaces cause more damage than those taken out in the open
D) To contemplate how a type of vocalization associated with positivity can actually represent both despair and longing
questions.question:
The following text is from the 1899 poem "Sympathy" by Paul Laurence Dunbar, who was a prominent African American poet born in Ohio.

I know why the caged bird sings, ah me, / When his wing is bruised and his bosom sore,— / When he beats his bars and he would be free; / It is not a carol of joy or glee, / But a prayer that he sends from his heart's deep core, / But a plea, that upward to Heaven he flings— / I know why the caged bird sings!

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the speaker explicitly states that the bird's singing—an act normally associated with joy—is "not a carol of joy or glee" but instead "a prayer" and "a plea" sent from a place of suffering. The poem's purpose is to reflect on how singing, generally understood as a happy sound, can actually express despair and a longing for freedom. Choice A is incorrect because the poem never compares how frequently glee versus hopelessness is perceived; it focuses on reinterpreting one specific vocalization (singing), not on comparing the frequency of emotions. Choice B is incorrect because the poem is told entirely from the caged bird's perspective and does not present or compare the perceptions of free people to those of imprisoned ones. Choice C is incorrect because the poem does not address or compare the amount of damage caused by actions in confined versus open spaces; its focus is on the meaning behind the bird's song, not on damage or action.

choices: A) It characterizes the rapidity with which the speaker questions himself.
B) It contrasts the speaker's feelings with the expectations of those around him.
C) It highlights the helplessness the speaker feels about the direction of his life.
D) It demonstrates the speaker's optimism that his questions will be eventually answered.
questions.question:
The following text is from the 1849 poem "Self-Dependence" by Matthew Arnold.

Weary of myself, and sick of asking / What I am, and what I ought to be, / At this vessel's prow I stand, which bears me / Forwards, forwards, o'er the starlit sea. / And a look of passionate desire / O'er the sea and to the stars I send: / "Ye who from my childhood up have calm'd me, / Calm me, ah, compose me to the end!

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion ("At this vessel's prow I stand, which bears me / Forwards, forwards, o'er the starlit sea.") in the text as a whole?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because the underlined lines depict the speaker as a passive figure standing at the prow while the vessel—not the speaker himself—is what "bears" him forward. Combined with the opening lines, in which the speaker is "weary" and "sick of asking" who he is and what he ought to be, this image of being carried forward by forces outside his control conveys the speaker's sense of helplessness over the course and direction of his own life. Choice A is incorrect because the lines describe the speaker being physically carried across the sea, not describe how quickly or repeatedly he questions himself; the repetition of "forwards, forwards" refers to the ship's movement, not the pace of his self-questioning. Choice B is incorrect because the lines make no mention of other people or their expectations; they focus solely on the speaker's own physical and emotional state aboard the ship. Choice D is incorrect because the passive, weary tone of being merely carried along by the vessel does not convey optimism; rather than suggesting confidence that his questions will be answered, the imagery reinforces the speaker's uncertainty and lack of control.

choices: A) It explains that a character is desperate to solve a problem, and then details how another character solves it.
B) It lists a character's concerns about his public image, and then explains how the character addresses these concerns.
C) It discloses the inspiration behind the actions of a character, and then describes why the character feels this way.
D) It details the speaker's attempt to emulate another character's behavior, and then underscores that the speaker was not as effective as the other character.
questions.question:
The following text is adapted from Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's 1905 novel The Return of Sherlock Holmes. Sherlock Holmes is a detective who uses his skills of deduction to solve crimes. His friend and partner, John Watson, narrates the novel.

It can be imagined that my close intimacy with Sherlock Holmes had interested me deeply in crime, and that after his disappearance I never failed to read with care the various problems which came before the public. There were points about this strange business which would, I was sure, have specially appealed to him, and the efforts of the police would have been supplemented, or more probably anticipated, by the trained observation and the alert mind of the first criminal agent in Europe. And I even attempted, more than once, for my own private satisfaction, to employ his methods in their solution, though with indifferent success.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the text first describes how Watson (the speaker) attempted to imitate Holmes's methods of deduction ("I even attempted... to employ his methods in their solution") and then explicitly notes that this attempt was less successful than Holmes himself would have been ("though with indifferent success," and the earlier statement that the police's efforts would have been "supplemented" or "anticipated" by Holmes's superior skill). Choice A is incorrect because the text does not describe another character solving a problem; it only discusses Watson's personal attempts and his belief that Holmes could have handled the cases better, without depicting an actual resolution by another character. Choice B is incorrect because the text is not concerned with Watson's public image or concerns about how he is perceived; it centers on his private interest in crime and his personal attempts to use Holmes's methods. Choice C is incorrect because the passage does not explain the inspiration behind actions and then explore the character's feelings about that inspiration—it recounts an attempted imitation and its limited success, not a psychological exploration of motivation.

choices: A) To recall a particular memory of a young bird safely navigating a storm
B) To emphasize the importance of remaining optimistic in the core of one's being
C) To bring awareness to life's challenges and the specific methods needed to overcome them
D) To claim that certain music can promote a diverse assortment of positive emotions
questions.question:
The following text is from Emily Dickinson's 1891 poem "Hope."

"Hope" is the thing with feathers – / That perches in the soul – / And sings the tune without the words – / And never stops – at all – / And sweetest – in the Gale – is heard – / And sore must be the storm – / That could abash the little Bird / That kept so many warm –

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.explanation: Choice B is the best answer because the poem personifies hope as a bird that "perches in the soul" and "never stops" singing, even during a "Gale" or storm, emphasizing that hope persists deep within a person no matter how difficult circumstances become—this conveys the importance of maintaining optimism at one's core. Choice A is incorrect because the poem is an extended metaphor about hope in general, not a recollection of one specific memory of an actual young bird surviving a storm. Choice C is incorrect because the poem does not detail specific methods for overcoming life's challenges; it simply describes hope's persistent, comforting presence without offering practical strategies. Choice D is incorrect because the poem focuses on hope itself, symbolized by the bird's song, rather than making a broader claim about music in general or its ability to produce a variety of positive emotions.

choices: A) Meg spends a long time getting ready each day in order to delay her responsibilities.
B) Meg feels quite overwhelmed with the prospect of caring for her sisters.
C) Meg remains calm and collected to help ease her family's burden.
D) Meg is becoming resentful of having to work on her appearance each day.
questions.question:
The following is text adapted from Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel Little Women. Meg, the oldest daughter in her family, often helps her mother with caring for her younger sisters.

This idea tickled Jo's fancy and put her in good spirits, but Meg didn't brighten, for her burden, consisting of four spoiled children, seemed heavier than ever. She had not heart enough even to make herself pretty as usual by putting on a blue neck ribbon and dressing her hair in the most becoming way.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.explanation: Choice B is the best answer because the text states that Meg's "burden"—caring for "four spoiled children"—"seemed heavier than ever," and that she lacked even the energy or heart to attend to her own appearance as she normally would. Both details show that Meg feels overwhelmed by the responsibility of caring for her sisters. Choice A is incorrect because the text says the opposite: Meg does not spend time on her appearance, rather she lacks the heart to do so, so this cannot be a delay tactic. Choice C is incorrect because the text shows Meg as weighed down and unhappy ("didn't brighten"), not calm and collected. Choice D is incorrect because the text does not describe resentment toward her own appearance routine; rather, it shows that her exhaustion from caregiving prevents her from maintaining her usual appearance.

choices: A) Despite their great success, the novels written by Jane Austen were not attributed to her due to a personal choice based on societal expectations.
B) Publishing anonymous novels like those written by Austen is the most efficient method to avoid judgments based on gender.
C) Although publishing works anonymously and maintaining secrecy such as Austen did can prevent societal criticism, it is unethical.
D) As an author, Austen was routinely encouraged by her friends and family members to take public credit for her works.
questions.question:
Because of the widespread belief in the early nineteenth century that it was improper for women to engage in literary careers, Jane Austen published her novels anonymously and did not reveal the secret of her authorship. Only her family members knew what she had written; this remained the case even as her novels gained popularity. The secret was rigorously kept: friends who came to visit and discuss her latest novels did not know they were speaking about them with the woman who had written them.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the text explains that Austen chose to publish anonymously ("did not reveal the secret of her authorship") specifically because of the era's societal belief that it was improper for women to have literary careers, and that this secrecy persisted "even as her novels gained popularity"—i.e., despite her success. Choice B is incorrect because the text does not make a general claim about anonymous publishing being the "most efficient method" for anyone facing gender-based judgment; it only describes Austen's specific personal choice. Choice C is incorrect because the text never characterizes Austen's choice to remain anonymous as unethical; it simply reports the fact and reasoning behind her secrecy without passing moral judgment. Choice D is incorrect because the text states the opposite: her secret was "rigorously kept," and even her friends did not know she was the author, meaning she was not being routinely encouraged by friends and family to take public credit—only her family knew at all, and there's no mention of anyone urging her to reveal herself.

choices: A) "Much have I seen and known; cities of men."
B) "How dull it is to pause, to make an end."
C) "Some work of noble note, may yet be done."
D) "Come, my friends, 'tis not too late to seek a newer world."
questions.question:
"Ulysses" is an 1842 poem by Alfred, Lord Tennyson. In the poem, Tennyson describes a king who proclaims his desire to travel once more, which he expresses to his companions, saying ________

Which quotation from "Ulysses" most effectively illustrates the claim?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly addresses the king's companions ("my friends") and explicitly expresses his desire to travel again, urging them to "seek a newer world" together, which precisely matches the claim that the king expresses his wish to travel once more to his companions. Choice A is incorrect because it only reflects on places the king has already seen in the past; it does not express a desire to travel again or address his companions directly. Choice B is incorrect because while it expresses dissatisfaction with stopping, it does not explicitly state a desire to travel or address his companions. Choice C is incorrect because it speaks generally about accomplishing some noble deed in the future, but it does not specifically reference travel or explicitly address his companions about a journey.

choices: A) For these four nations, Costa Rica and Panama had the lowest percentage of people working in the agricultural sector and the lowest percentage of people living in urban areas.
B) For these four nations, the nation with the highest percentage of people in the agricultural sector also had the highest percentage of people in urban areas.
C) Belize demonstrated a similar percentage of people in the agricultural sector to El Salvador's despite having a lower percentage of people in urban areas.
D) El Salvador and Panama had similar percentages of people in the agricultural sector, but Panama had a higher percentage of people in urban areas than El Salvador did.
questions.question:
Percentages of Population Working in the Agricultural Sector and Living in Urban Areas for Four Central American Nations
NationPercentage working in the agricultural sectorPercentage living in urban areas
Belize16.8045.87
Costa Rica11.9780.08
El Salvador16.2972.75
Panama14.4168.06
A group of researchers conducted a study of four Central American nations to explore the relationship between the percentage of the population working in the agricultural sector and the percentage of the population living in urban areas. Although the percentages of those living in urban areas varied significantly, the percentages of those working in the agricultural sector did not vary as greatly. The group claimed that, for these four nations, there is not a strong correlation between where people work and where they live. Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' claim?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it identifies two nations, Belize (16.80%) and El Salvador (16.29%), that have very similar percentages of people working in the agricultural sector, yet have quite different percentages of people living in urban areas (45.87% versus 72.75%). This shows that a similar agricultural-sector percentage does not correspond to a similar urban-living percentage, directly supporting the claim that there is no strong correlation between the two variables. Choice A is incorrect because it merely states which two nations had the lowest values in each category without showing whether similar or different agricultural percentages correspond to similar or different urban percentages—it does not demonstrate a lack of correlation. Choice B is incorrect because it actually describes a pattern where agricultural and urban percentages move together (the highest of one corresponds to the highest of the other), which would suggest a correlation, undermining rather than supporting the researchers' claim. Choice D is incorrect because it describes two nations, El Salvador and Panama, whose agricultural percentages are similar (16.29 vs. 14.41) but whose urban percentages differ modestly (72.75 vs. 68.06)—this contrast is far less stark than the one in Choice C and does not as clearly demonstrate the lack of correlation, since Costa Rica's data (lowest agricultural percentage, highest urban percentage) shows the numbers were not even used to their full contrastive potential compared to the Belize/El Salvador pairing.

choices: A) The largest increase in words given to the subjects occurred from Trial 1 to Trial 4.
B) The number of words recited in Trial 3 was greater than the number of words given in Trial 3.
C) The words recited by the subjects still increased in Trial 4 despite an increase from Trial 3 in the words given.
D) The words given and the words recited were the same in Trial 2.
questions.question:
Words Recited Based on Word Count (bar graph showing, for Trials 1 through 4, the average number of words given and the average number of words recited)

To determine how many items a person can hold in their short-term memory, a psychologist gave four subjects word lists in four different trials and asked them to memorize and then recite the words on the list. The list in each trial contained a different number of words. The psychologist concluded that there is a limit to the number of items people can hold in their short-term memory.

Which choice best describes data from the graph that weaken the psychologist's conclusion?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because if the number of words recited kept increasing in Trial 4 even as the number of words given also increased from Trial 3, this suggests that the subjects had not yet hit a maximum capacity—their recall kept pace with the increasing list length rather than plateauing at some fixed limit. This directly weakens the conclusion that there is a hard limit to short-term memory capacity. Choice A is incorrect because it only describes a change in the number of words given to subjects, not their recall performance, so it says nothing about whether a memory limit exists. Choice B is incorrect because it is not a meaningful or even plausible way to weaken the conclusion—subjects cannot recite more words than they were given, so this comparison does not provide evidence about a memory ceiling. Choice D is incorrect because showing that given and recited words matched in Trial 2 (likely a trial with a small word count) does not address whether a ceiling exists at higher word counts, so it fails to weaken the specific conclusion about there being an upper limit.

choices: A) decrease the cost of postage for letters that contain only news and information.
B) provide news and information to everyone, especially those in lower classes.
C) transform the common relationship between wealth and the privilege of postage use.
D) encourage members of lower classes considering a post office job to apply for a newspaper position instead.
questions.question:
Although postage for letters in the early United States was expensive and therefore largely limited to the wealthy, politicians such as James Madison believed that money raised by the postal system could be used to benefit the nation as a whole. Madison proposed that a possible application of these funds toward the purpose of benefitting young Americans was the establishment of a newspaper for the general public, which would therefore ________

Which choice most logically completes the text?
questions.explanation: Choice B is the best answer because the passage establishes that expensive postage limited access to information to the wealthy, and that Madison wanted to use postal funds to benefit the nation "as a whole," including young Americans. A newspaper "for the general public" logically would provide news and information to everyone, particularly the lower classes who were previously excluded by the high cost of postage. Choice A is incorrect because the passage is about funding a new public newspaper, not about reducing the cost of existing letter postage; nothing suggests the plan targeted postage rates for news-only letters. Choice C is incorrect because while the newspaper might indirectly affect who has access to information, the passage does not suggest that Madison's specific proposal was intended to "transform" the wealth-postage relationship as a whole—his aim, as stated, was benefiting the public through a newspaper, not policy reform of postage privilege itself. Choice D is incorrect because there is no mention in the text of encouraging lower-class individuals to switch from postal jobs to newspaper jobs; this idea is entirely unsupported by the passage.

choices: A) theories and the lack of
B) theories and the lack of,
C) theories, and the lack of,
D) theories, and, the lack of
questions.question:
Pinpointing the exact cause of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) has been difficult due to the absence of conclusive proof for any of the proposed ________ a clear diagnostic test for the condition.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the sentence is built around a single prepositional phrase, "due to," with two objects joined by "and": "the absence of conclusive proof for any of the proposed theories" and "the lack of a clear diagnostic test for the condition." Because this is a simple two-item compound (X and Y) rather than a list of three or more items or two independent clauses, no comma is needed before or after "and," and no comma should separate the preposition "of" from its object "a clear diagnostic test." Choice B is incorrect because it inserts a comma after "of," incorrectly separating the preposition from its object noun phrase. Choice C is incorrect because it adds an unnecessary comma before "and" (which is not needed for a simple two-item compound) as well as the same incorrect comma after "of" seen in Choice B. Choice D is incorrect because it adds unneeded commas both before and after "and," as well as after "of," needlessly fragmenting the phrase and disrupting its grammatical structure.

choices: A) historians Diodorus Siculus, and Quintus Rufus
B) historians, Diodorus Siculus and Quintus Rufus,
C) historians, Diodorus Siculus and Quintus Rufus
D) historians Diodorus Siculus and Quintus Rufus
questions.question:
Persepolis was an ancient city in the First Persian Empire, located in what is now Iran. Ancient ________ claimed that Alexander the Great had purposely burned down the city's structures after he and his army had conquered Persepolis in 330 BCE.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because "Diodorus Siculus and Quintus Rufus" functions as a restrictive (essential) appositive that specifies exactly which historians are being discussed—without these names, "Ancient historians" would be too vague to identify who made the claim. Because the appositive is essential to the sentence's meaning, it should not be set off by any commas. Choice A is incorrect because it inserts an unnecessary comma before "and," incorrectly separating the two names in what should be a simple two-item list within the appositive. Choice B is incorrect because it sets off the appositive with commas on both sides, treating it as nonessential extra information, when in fact the names are essential to specifying which historians are meant. Choice C is incorrect because it includes a comma before the appositive but not after it, creating inconsistent and grammatically incorrect punctuation—since the appositive is restrictive, it should have no commas at all, not just one.

questions.question:
Homer was an ancient Greek poet who lived during the 8th century BCE, but he is not the world's earliest known author. During the 23rd century BCE in ancient Mesopotamia, Enheduanna, a high priestess, wrote poems and ________ during the 24th century BCE in ancient Egypt, a government official named Ptahhotep wrote aphorisms and maxims intended to guide young people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because the sentence contains two independent clauses: "Enheduanna...wrote poems and hymns" and "during the 24th century BCE in ancient Egypt, a government official named Ptahhotep wrote aphorisms and maxims...." Two independent clauses must be joined either with a comma and coordinating conjunction, a period, or a semicolon; here, a semicolon is the correct choice to link the two closely related independent clauses. Choice A is incorrect because it creates a comma splice, joining two independent clauses with only commas (and an inserted word "earlier"), which is not grammatically permitted. Choice B is incorrect for the same reason—it joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, resulting in a comma splice. Choice D is incorrect because it also joins the two independent clauses with only a comma and no coordinating conjunction, again creating a comma splice.

questions.question:
Although it is often assumed that one of the essential characteristics of mammals is that they give live birth to their young, there are actually two species of egg-laying ________ Ornithorhynchus anatinus, more commonly known as the duck-billed platypus, and Tachyglossus aculeatus, also called a short-beaked echidna or spiny anteater.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because a colon is used to introduce a list or explanation that elaborates on the preceding independent clause. Here, "there are actually two species of egg-laying mammals" is a complete independent clause, and the colon correctly introduces the two specific species that make up that claim. Choice B is incorrect because a period would require what follows to be a complete, independent sentence, but "Ornithorhynchus anatinus...and Tachyglossus aculeatus..." has no main verb and is a sentence fragment, not a complete sentence. Choice C is incorrect because a semicolon must join two independent clauses, but what follows the semicolon is not an independent clause—it lacks a verb and is simply a list of two species. Choice D is incorrect because using no punctuation at all creates a run-on, failing to clearly signal that a list explaining "mammals" follows.

choices: A) the praise from many historians has been for Worth's pioneering work in high-end dressmaking; they
B) many historians have praised Worth as a pioneer of high-end dressmaking and
C) Worth's pioneering work in high-end dressmaking has been praised by many historians, who
D) there are many historians who have praised Worth as a pioneer of high-end dressmaking, and they
questions.question:
In analyzing the designs, career, and legacy of English fashion designer Charles Frederick Worth, ________ have declared him to be the first modern fashion designer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice B is the best answer because the sentence opens with the introductory participial phrase "In analyzing the designs, career, and legacy of...Worth," which must be immediately followed by the noun performing that analyzing action to avoid a dangling modifier. Only "many historians" can logically be the ones doing the analyzing, and Choice B correctly places "many historians" as the subject, followed by two parallel verbs ("have praised...and [have] declared"). Choice A is incorrect because it creates a dangling modifier: "the praise" cannot logically be the one "analyzing" Worth's designs, career, and legacy. Choice C is incorrect for the same reason—"Worth's pioneering work" cannot be the entity doing the analyzing described in the introductory phrase. Choice D is incorrect because it places "there" as the subject of the analyzing action, which is also illogical and creates a dangling modifier, since "there" cannot analyze anything.

choices: A) Audible, in 2008, a live streaming platform,
B) Audible; in 2008, a live streaming platform;
C) Audible; in 2008, a live streaming platform,
D) Audible, in 2008; a live streaming platform,
questions.question:
Amazon, one of the largest technology companies in the world, was founded in 1994 as an online bookstore and has gone on to acquire a seller of audiobooks, ________ Twitch, in 2014; and a supermarket chain, Whole Foods Market, in 2017.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the sentence presents a list of three acquisitions, each written as a category followed by a specific name and year (e.g., "a seller of audiobooks, Audible, in 2008"). Because each list item already contains internal commas, semicolons are needed to separate the three items from one another so the list is not confusing; Choice D correctly places a semicolon after "in 2008" to close the first item ("a seller of audiobooks, Audible, in 2008") before starting the next item ("a live streaming platform, Twitch, in 2014"). Choice A is incorrect because it uses only commas throughout, making it impossible to tell where one list item ends and the next begins, since each item already contains commas of its own. Choice B is incorrect because it places a semicolon right after "Audible," incorrectly severing the name "Audible" from its accompanying year "in 2008," which are part of the same list item. Choice C is incorrect for the same reason as Choice B—it places the semicolon too early, splitting "Audible" from "in 2008" within the same item, while also being inconsistent by using a comma instead of a semicolon later in the list.

questions.question:
Scientists have used common materials, including aluminum, sulfur, and salt, to create a new type of battery. Lithium-ion batteries were the most popular battery in the past, but they are becoming harder and more expensive to make due to a shortage of lithium. ________ the new battery provides many benefits: it is low-cost, it is able to resist failures and fires, and it charges faster than typical batteries do.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the previous sentence describes a problem with lithium-ion batteries (they are becoming "harder and more expensive to make"), while the sentence with the blank describes the advantages of the new battery (low-cost, safe, fast-charging). "In comparison" correctly signals that the new battery is being contrasted with the previously mentioned lithium-ion batteries. Choice B is incorrect because "What's more" signals an additional point in the same direction as the previous sentence, but the previous sentence described a negative (a shortage-driven problem), while this sentence describes positives—these are not simply additive points. Choice C is incorrect because "Similarly" signals that the new information is alike to what preceded it, but the new battery's benefits are being contrasted with, not compared favorably to, the drawbacks of lithium-ion batteries. Choice D is incorrect for the same reason as Choice B—"In addition" implies simply adding a similar point rather than drawing the necessary contrast between the problems of one battery type and the benefits of another.

choices: A) The viola is a string instrument, and the flute is a woodwind instrument.
B) The concertos, or musical compositions for a soloist and an ensemble, were both written by Stamitz in the late 1700s.
C) Stamitz wrote numerous concertos, including one for viola and one for flute.
D) While both were written by Stamitz, the 1774 concerto is for viola, and the 1780 concerto is for flute.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Anton Stamitz was a composer.
• He wrote symphonies, string quartets, and concertos.
• A concerto is a musical composition for a soloist and an ensemble.
• Stamitz wrote a concerto for viola, a string instrument, in 1774.
• He wrote a concerto for flute, a woodwind instrument, in 1780.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two concertos. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly sets up a contrast between the two specific concertos, using "while" to acknowledge their shared authorship before highlighting their differing instruments and years ("the 1774 concerto is for viola, and the 1780 concerto is for flute"), which directly accomplishes the goal of emphasizing a difference. Choice A is incorrect because it only states general facts about instrument categories without tying them back to the two specific concertos or Stamitz, failing to frame this as a difference between his two works. Choice B is incorrect because it emphasizes a similarity (both written by Stamitz in the late 1700s) rather than a difference between the concertos. Choice C is incorrect because it simply lists that Stamitz wrote concertos including ones for viola and flute, without explicitly contrasting the two works or framing this as a notable difference.

choices: A) Both the Pyramid of Menkaure, which is located in Egypt, and the Pyramid of the Sun, which is located in what is now Mexico, are examples of ancient pyramids.
B) Some of the world's pyramids, including one that is thought to have been built around 200 CE by the ancient Teotihuacanos, are taller than 200 feet.
C) The Pyramid of Menkaure is 213 feet tall, while the slightly taller Pyramid of the Sun is 216 feet tall.
D) The Pyramid of Menkaure, which is 213 feet tall, is thought to have been built in the 26th century BCE by the ancient Egyptians.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Pyramid of Menkaure is a pyramid in Egypt.
• It is thought to have been built in the 26th century BCE by the ancient Egyptians.
• It is 213 feet tall.
• The Pyramid of the Sun is a pyramid in what is now Mexico.
• It is thought to have been built around 200 CE by the ancient Teotihuacanos.
• It is 216 feet tall.

The student wants to compare the heights of the two pyramids. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it directly states the height of each pyramid (213 feet and 216 feet) and explicitly compares them using "while the slightly taller," fulfilling the goal of comparing the two pyramids' heights. Choice A is incorrect because it discusses the pyramids' locations, not their heights, and does not accomplish the stated goal. Choice B is incorrect because it only mentions that some pyramids, including the Pyramid of the Sun, are taller than 200 feet, without directly comparing its height to the Pyramid of Menkaure's specific height. Choice D is incorrect because it only provides the height of the Pyramid of Menkaure and mentions its construction date, without mentioning or comparing it to the height of the Pyramid of the Sun at all.

choices: A) When the ocean's pH levels decrease, there is decreased net calcification.
B) Coral reefs are held together by net calcification, which has decreased in some places.
C) Net calcification holds coral reefs together, and carbon dioxide emissions have reduced the ocean's pH levels.
D) Net calcification has decreased in some coral reefs as a result of a decrease in the ocean's pH levels.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Coral reefs are ocean ecosystems that are held together by a process called net calcification.
• Some coral reefs have exhibited decreased net calcification.
• Carbon dioxide emissions cause the ocean's pH levels to decrease.
• A decrease in the ocean's pH levels results in decreased net calcification.

The student wants to specify the reason that some coral reefs have changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly and explicitly states the cause-and-effect relationship the student wants to highlight: net calcification in some coral reefs has decreased "as a result of" a decrease in ocean pH levels, specifying the exact reason for the coral reefs' change. Choice A is incorrect because it states a general relationship between pH and calcification without connecting it specifically to the change in coral reefs mentioned in the notes. Choice B is incorrect because it notes that net calcification has decreased in some places but does not specify the reason (the pH decrease) behind that change. Choice C is incorrect because, although it mentions both net calcification and the pH-lowering effect of carbon dioxide, it does not explicitly connect these two facts as cause and effect for the change in coral reefs—it merely lists them as separate statements.

choices: A) It has been assumed that insects migrate in a random fashion, so researchers from the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior studied the migratory habits of hawkmoths.
B) Researchers from the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior tagged and monitored hawkmoths, which, like mosquitos, butterflies, bees, and locusts, are migratory animals.
C) Trillions of animals migrate through the air each year; recently, one such animal was tagged and monitored.
D) The study's surprising results demonstrated that rather than migrating in a random fashion, as was previously assumed, hawkmoths exhibit sophisticated flight strategies.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Each year, trillions of animals migrate by flying through the air.
• Insects, such as mosquitos, butterflies, bees, locusts, and moths, are among the most common migratory animals.
• It has been assumed that insects migrate in a random fashion, being heavily impacted by the changing winds.
• Researchers from the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior led a study in which hawkmoths were tagged and monitored as they migrated from Germany to the Alps.
• The study's surprising results demonstrated that the hawkmoths have more sophisticated flight strategies than previously thought.

The student wants to emphasize the study's significance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly states that the study's results were "surprising" and explicitly contrasts the prior assumption (random migration driven by wind) with the actual finding (sophisticated flight strategies), which is exactly what conveys the significance of the study's findings. Choice A is incorrect because it only explains the assumption that motivated the study and the fact that the study occurred, without ever mentioning the results or why they mattered. Choice B is incorrect because it simply describes the study's methodology (tagging and monitoring) and lists other migratory insects, without addressing the results or their significance. Choice C is incorrect because it offers only a generic statement about animal migration and vaguely mentions that "one such animal" was studied, without specifying any results or their importance.

choices: A) Krishnamurthy's novel is set in India during the Chola Dynasty, while Proust's is set in early 20th-century France.
B) Krishnamurthy, an Indian author, published his novel in the 1950s; Proust, a French author, published his between 1913 and 1927.
C) Although both Krishnamurthy's and Proust's novels tell the life stories of two men, the settings of the two novels are quite different.
D) Krishnamurthy's and Proust's novels are both epic at 2,210 pages and 4,215 pages, respectively.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the 1950s, Indian author Kalki Krishnamurthy published The Son of Ponni.
• His epic novel (2,210 pages) tells the story of Prince Arulmozhivarman, an emperor of the Chola Dynasty in India.
• Between 1913 and 1927, French author Marcel Proust published In Search of Lost Time.
• In Proust's epic novel (4,215 pages), a narrator reflects on his memories.
• The novel explores the transformation of early 20th-century French society.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two novels. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly states the shared trait that both novels are "epic," or extremely long, giving their respective page counts (2,210 and 4,215) as supporting detail, which clearly emphasizes a similarity between the two works. Choice A is incorrect because it highlights a difference in setting between the two novels, not a similarity. Choice B is incorrect because it simply lists separate facts about each author's nationality and publication dates without connecting them as a similarity; the parallel structure describes two different things (different countries, different date ranges) rather than a shared trait. Choice C is incorrect because, although it briefly mentions a similarity (life stories of two men), its main emphasis is on a difference ("the settings of the two novels are quite different"), which works against the goal of emphasizing similarity.

choices: A) Persuaded by sensationalist journalism, Americans came to favor war with Spain, and then the United States declared war.
B) The newspaper publishers Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst competed with each other using sensationalist coverage.
C) The newspapers run by Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst were highly critical of Spain.
D) In 1898, the United States declared war on Spain, which had been blamed for the sinking of a US battleship.
questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the 1890s, newspaper publishers Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst were competitors.
• Their newspapers used sensationalist coverage to drive sales.
• One issue that was sensationally covered was the tyrannical manner in which Spain ruled its then colony of Cuba.
• Another issue was the sinking of a US battleship near Cuba, which the newspapers blamed on Spain without evidence.
• The newspapers' coverage persuaded Americans to favor war, and in 1898, the United States declared war on Spain.

The student wants to emphasize the role that journalism played in a declaration of war. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it directly and explicitly connects sensationalist journalism to the outcome of a declared war, tracing the causal chain from being "persuaded by sensationalist journalism" to Americans favoring war to the United States actually declaring war—this precisely emphasizes journalism's role in the declaration of war. Choice B is incorrect because it only describes the competition between the two publishers and their use of sensationalist coverage, without connecting this to the declaration of war at all. Choice C is incorrect because it only states that the newspapers were critical of Spain, without linking this coverage to Americans' opinions or to the actual declaration of war. Choice D is incorrect because it focuses on the declaration of war and the blame placed on Spain for the battleship's sinking, but never mentions journalism, newspapers, or the media's role in shaping public opinion.

questions.question:
Regarded as a founder of medical microbiology, Louis Pasteur was a researcher at the University of Lille in 1854. There, Pasteur discovered that passing oxygen through a fluid could stop its fermentation, creating an environment that was no longer ________ bacteria growth.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it creates the most logical cause-and-effect relationship in the sentence. Pasteur discovered that passing oxygen through a fluid stopped fermentation, which is itself driven by bacterial (microbial) activity. If fermentation stops, the environment is no longer "conducive to," or supportive/promoting of, bacteria growth. "No longer conducive to" precisely captures the idea that a condition that once encouraged growth has been removed.

Choice A is incorrect because "available for" does not capture the idea of promoting or encouraging growth; an environment can be "available for" something without actively fostering it, so the phrase does not precisely convey what oxygen's effect was.

Choice B is incorrect because "reminiscent of" means "reminding one of" or "similar to," which makes no logical sense in the context of an environment either supporting or not supporting a biological process like bacterial growth.

Choice C is incorrect because it reverses the intended logic: if the environment were "no longer inhospitable to" bacteria growth, that would mean the environment became newly welcoming to growth, which contradicts the point that oxygen stopped fermentation (a bacterial process).

questions.question:
Completed in 1937, Metamorphosis of Narcissus was Salvador Dalí's interpretation of the Greek myth of Narcissus. Known for his ________ style, Dalí painted Metamorphosis in accordance with the paranoiac critical method, a surrealist technique he created and named himself, in which he worked in a paranoid state to find connections between objects that are not rationally linked.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because the text describes a highly unconventional artistic method: Dalí invented and named his own technique, worked in a self-induced paranoid state, and searched for connections between objects that are "not rationally linked." This description of a self-created, unusual approach to art is best captured by "eccentric," meaning unconventional or odd.

Choice A is incorrect because "unfathomable" means impossible to understand or comprehend, but the text goes on to clearly explain and describe Dalí's method in detail, meaning it is not something incomprehensible.

Choice B is incorrect because "orthodox" means conventional or traditional, which is the opposite of the self-invented, unconventional method the text describes.

Choice D is incorrect because "unreliable" describes something that cannot be trusted or depended on, but the text does not suggest that Dalí's style or method was untrustworthy—only that it was unusual.

questions.question:
Modern reviews of Mozart's opera The Marriage of Figaro typically praise the uprising of the opera's lower class individuals against unfair treatment ________ by the Spanish nobility. Most other operas set during this period end in tragedy, with the members of the lower class having their desires crushed by the corrupt noblemen and women, though Figaro is a memorable deviation from this norm.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because the sentence describes an uprising against "unfair treatment" that comes from "the Spanish nobility," and the surrounding context describes the nobility as "corrupt" and crushing the desires of the lower class. This indicates that the nobility actively caused, or "inflicted," this unfair treatment upon the lower class.

Choice B is incorrect because "interrupted" would mean the nobility briefly stopped the unfair treatment, which does not match the context describing the nobility as the source of oppression that the lower class rises up against.

Choice C is incorrect because "accomplished" suggests the nobility successfully achieved or completed the unfair treatment as a goal, which does not fit as naturally as the idea that the nobility caused or imposed this treatment upon others.

Choice D is incorrect because "explained" would mean the nobility provided a rationale or reason for the unfair treatment, but the text is not about the nobility justifying their actions—it is about them causing harm that the lower class rises up against.

questions.question:
Throughout her novels, rather than merely ________ the issues surrounding inequality, Toni Morrison uses specific techniques: intricate language, with its ability to describe horrific situations; flashbacks and stories, clearly depicting miscarriages of justice; and vivid imagery, revealing the savagery that one group unleashed upon another.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because the sentence sets up a contrast ("rather than merely ________") between a shallow, surface-level treatment of inequality and the deep, vivid techniques Morrison actually uses (intricate language, flashbacks, vivid imagery) to fully depict and reveal these issues. "Referencing" describes a light, passing mention of a topic, which contrasts appropriately with the elaborate, immersive techniques listed afterward.

Choice A is incorrect because "substituting" implies replacing the issues of inequality with something else entirely, which does not logically contrast with actively depicting those issues through detailed techniques.

Choice B is incorrect because "confusing" the issues would mean making them unclear or muddled, which is not a logical alternative to the vivid, clarifying techniques described in the rest of the sentence.

Choice C is incorrect because "supplementing" means adding to or complementing something, which does not fit the contrast structure of "rather than merely ________"—the sentence needs a word describing a minimal or surface treatment that Morrison moves beyond, not an additive one.

choices: A) By disagreeing with the claim that human beings are shaped only by external stimuli that become learned behavior
B) By admitting that external stimuli play an important part in the development of the subconscious through association
C) By questioning the belief that the development of the id is dependent upon learning from the consequences of a behavior
D) By confirming that the innate human mind does not develop until exposure to external stimuli
questions.question:
Text 1

According to the theory of classical conditioning, humans are controlled by external stimuli within their environment, which trigger responses and then patterns of new, learned behavior in an individual. Some psychologists who champion classical conditioning believe that there is no innate human mind at all and that people's behaviors are solely a result of the stimuli they experience: different experiences lead to different responses and, ultimately, different personalities.

Text 2

Throughout his career, psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud argued that the decisions humans make are governed by their unconscious mind, which consists of three components—the id, ego, and superego—that each play a significant role in human behavior. Freud's argument was based on the concept that humans must possess certain instinctual impulses at birth based on observations of young children attempting to learn control over those impulses.

Based on the texts, how would Freud (Text 2) most likely respond to the idea of "classical conditioning" presented in Text 1?
questions.explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because Text 2 explains that Freud believed humans possess certain "instinctual impulses at birth," meaning behavior is not purely learned from external stimuli. This directly conflicts with the classical conditioning view in Text 1 that "there is no innate human mind at all" and that behavior is "solely a result of the stimuli" people experience. Since Freud's theory rests on innate, inborn impulses, he would disagree with the claim that humans are shaped only by external, learned stimuli.

Choice B is incorrect because Freud's theory as described emphasizes innate, instinctual impulses present at birth, not that the subconscious develops through learned association with external stimuli; admitting this would contradict his own argument.

Choice C is incorrect because Text 2 does not suggest the id develops through learning from consequences—rather, it states the id-related instinctual impulses are present at birth, prior to any learning, so Freud would not need to question this since it isn't the classical conditioning claim being made.

Choice D is incorrect because it reverses Freud's actual view; Text 2 indicates Freud believed humans have instinctual impulses from birth, meaning the innate mind exists at birth already, not that it only develops after exposure to external stimuli.

choices: A) The evidence found by De Blasio and colleagues supports the idea of a tsunami occurring somewhere other than the Earth.
B) The evidence found by De Blasio and colleagues suggests that the Earth had larger tsunamis in the past than it does today.
C) The team's research assists researchers in investigating the idea that Mars may be more suitable for human life than was previously believed.
D) The team's research assists geologists in constructing an accurate timeline of topographical changes on Mars.
questions.question:
It has been long believed that Earth is the only planet in the solar system with tsunamis—series of waves generated by the displacement of a massive quantity of water such as an ocean or lake—that are often caused by mountain landslides. In an article that aims to broaden our current scope of knowledge regarding tsunamis, scientist Fabio Vittorio De Blasio and colleagues released research describing evidence of a massive landslide, which left a path of destruction so lengthy that it could only have been caused by a massive volume of water, originating on Mars's Olympus Mons.

According to the text, why was De Blasio and his colleagues' research on the Olympus Mons landslide significant?
questions.explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because the text states it was "long believed that Earth is the only planet in the solar system with tsunamis" but that De Blasio and colleagues found evidence of a landslide on Mars whose destruction path was so extensive it "could only have been caused by a massive volume of water"—the very mechanism that produces tsunamis. This directly supports the idea that a tsunami-like event occurred on a planet other than Earth, challenging the long-held belief.

Choice B is incorrect because the text makes no comparison between the size of past and present tsunamis on Earth; the research is about a landslide on Mars, not about Earth's tsunami history.

Choice C is incorrect because the text is about historical evidence of water-driven landslides on Mars, not about assessing Mars's current or future suitability for human habitation.

Choice D is incorrect because the text describes a single landslide as evidence of a past tsunami-like event, not as part of a broader effort to construct a timeline of topographical changes on Mars.

choices: A) She aspires to be more like her parents.
B) She desires the possessions and belongings of others.
C) Traveling to places is her preferred pastime.
D) Winter is her preferred time of year.
questions.question:
The following text is adapted from Carolyn Wells's 1905 novel Patty in the City.

The dining-room, too, excited Ethelyn's admiration. The soft thick carpets, and daintily laid tables, each with its vase of flowers, seemed suddenly to her far more desirable than the well-appointed dining-room in her own home at Villa Rosa.

Ethelyn was of an envious disposition, and though she was indulged and petted by her parents, she always wanted the belongings of someone else. She determined right then and there to coax her father to close up Villa Rosa and come to New York for the winter, though she had little hope that he would do so.

According to the text, what is true about Ethelyn?
questions.explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because the text explicitly states that Ethelyn "was of an envious disposition" and "always wanted the belongings of someone else." This is directly illustrated by the passage's opening: seeing another dining room made her own home's dining room seem less desirable by comparison, showing her tendency to covet what others have.

Choice A is incorrect because the text says Ethelyn was "indulged and petted by her parents," but there is no indication she wants to be more like them; her defining trait described in the text is envy of others' possessions, not admiration of her parents.

Choice C is incorrect because the text does not state that traveling is her preferred pastime; her wish to go to New York stems from wanting the dining room and lifestyle she saw there, not from a general love of travel.

Choice D is incorrect because Ethelyn wants to spend winter in New York specifically because of the appealing dining room and surroundings she observed, not because winter itself is her preferred season.

choices: A) It's challenging to determine the exact origins of Yellow Fever due to the disease's fatal nature.
B) Reed's experiment provided firm evidence for a colleague's theory about disease transmission.
C) Reed invented a novel approach for investigating the symptoms of exotic diseases.
D) Bloodwork is the most critical type of analysis needed for curing a patient with Yellow Fever.
questions.question:
In 1886 Carlos J. Finlay published experimental evidence positing that yellow fever was transmitted from infected mosquitoes to healthy humans. However, other researchers refused to acknowledge Finlay's theory, until Finlay finally convinced Walter Reed, the head physician of the US Army Yellow Fever board, to investigate further. Reed isolated a group of healthy volunteers who allowed an infected mosquito to bite them and then have their blood drawn, capturing the virus in a test tube. By injecting the drawn blood into other participants, Reed was able to show a successful transmission of Yellow Fever—the first concrete demonstration that the disease originates from infected mosquitoes.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
questions.explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because the text traces a clear arc: Finlay proposed a theory (mosquito-to-human transmission) that other researchers doubted, until Reed conducted an experiment that provided "the first concrete demonstration" confirming Finlay's theory. This is precisely what "Reed's experiment provided firm evidence for a colleague's theory about disease transmission" describes.

Choice A is incorrect because the text is not about the difficulty of determining Yellow Fever's origins or its fatality; it focuses on how Reed's experiment confirmed the mosquito-transmission theory.

Choice C is incorrect because the text is not primarily about Reed inventing a novel investigative method for exotic disease symptoms in general; it is about proving a specific existing theory of transmission for one disease.

Choice D is incorrect because while blood was used in Reed's experiment, the text does not claim bloodwork is "the most critical type of analysis needed for curing" Yellow Fever patients—the passage is about proving how the disease is transmitted, not about treatment or cures.

choices: A) “Every one suspects himself of at least one of the cardinal virtues, and this is mine: I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known.”

B) “And so with the sunshine and the great bursts of leaves growing on the trees, just as things grow in fast movies, I had that familiar conviction that life was beginning over again with the summer.”
C) “I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.”

D) “I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.”
questions.question:
The Great Gatsby is a 1925 novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald. In the novel, the narrator describes events surrounding Jay Gatsby and the elite social circles of East and West Egg. The novel contrasts the narrator's morality with the immorality of his social acquaintances, such as when the narrator says ________

Which quotation from The Great Gatsby most effectively illustrates the claim?
questions.explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it directly and explicitly states the narrator's claim to personal moral superiority: he calls honesty one of his own "cardinal virtues" and states outright, "I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known." This directly illustrates the contrast the claim describes between the narrator's own morality (his honesty) and the implied immorality of the people around him (since he considers himself one of only a "few" honest people among his acquaintances).

Choice B is incorrect because this quotation describes a seasonal, nostalgic feeling about summer beginning again; it does not address morality or immorality of the narrator or his acquaintances at all.

Choice C is incorrect because this quotation expresses the narrator's mixed emotional reaction (enchantment and repulsion) to the variety of life he witnesses, but it does not explicitly draw a contrast between his own morality and others' immorality.

Choice D is incorrect because this quotation discusses an inherited, unequal sense of "fundamental decencies" and calls the idea "snobbish," but it does not directly contrast the narrator's own moral behavior with the immoral behavior of his social acquaintances the way Choice A does.

choices: A) The approximate lifespans determined by the Fisheries biologist, Christiansen, and Ste-Marie et al. all fell within the approximated lifespan range determined by Nielsen et al., even though there were differences in the methods used by each of the four groups.

B) The study by the Fisheries biologist used tagging for measurements and produced the lowest approximated lifespan, while the study by Neilsen et al. used carbon dating and produced the highest approximated lifespan.
C) In their study, Ste-Marie et al. used metabolic rate and food consumption to determine the Greenland shark's lifespan approximation to be 500 years.

D) Though the lifespans approximated by the Fisheries biologist and Christiansen were identical to each other, the lifespans approximated by Ste-Marie et al. and Nielsen et al. differed significantly from any other approximation.
questions.question:
StudyYearEstimation methodApproximate lifespan (years)
Fisheries biologist1930Tagging and measuring growth each year400
Christiansen2009Satellite tagging and measurement of growth400
Nielsen et al.2016Carbon dating and analyzing eye protein400–600
